clauses.reason: The single clause (the reservation of the Sitka, Alaska lands for the Coast and Geodetic Survey as a magnetic and seismological observatory site) ended on 1941-08-16, when paragraph 1 of Executive Order 8854 revoked Executive Order 8168 of June 14, 1939 without condition. The date is the signing date of Executive Order 8854, which states no separate effective date and was filed on August 18 and published on August 20, 1941. Paragraph 2 of Executive Order 8854 separately reserves the same lands again, which is a new command and not a continuation of this clause. The held text shows no earlier ending.

research_rationale:
I read the complete held Federal Register original of Executive Order 8168 (4 FR 2415, June 16, 1939; signed June 14, 1939). After recitals that the Department of Agriculture no longer needed and had abandoned its Sitka, Alaska experiment-station lands, a single operative sentence revokes the Executive order of August 12, 1898 and reserves the lands for the Coast and Geodetic Survey of the Department of Commerce as a magnetic and seismological observatory site. It has no duration, condition or savings language. I read the complete held Federal Register text of Executive Order 8854 (6 FR 4181, August 20, 1941; signed August 16, 1941), titled as revoking Executive Order 8168. The Federal Register text layer renders the order number in the quotation as 81681 (a footnote mark run into the number); the actual checker reads that as a different order and reports a mechanical order-exists failure, which is an extraction artifact. An American Presidency Project transcription of the same order is held and agrees in substance, but an official copy is held, so the transcription may not be used as the quoted source. Paragraph 1 orders that Executive Order No. 8168 of June 14, 1939, is revoked, with no condition or exception. Paragraph 2 separately withdraws the lands contained in the 8168 reservation and an adjoining tract for the same Survey use under the President's own authority. Paragraph 2 is a new reservation made by Executive Order 8854, not a continuation of Executive Order 8168, so the whole of Executive Order 8168 ended on August 16, 1941. I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them: the U.S. Code search (through 2026-10-09) and the eCFR search (as of 2026-10-14) found no citation of this order, and the Federal Register disposition-note search found only the revocation by Executive Order 8854 (two catalog entries for the same event). The Federal Register text layer is machine extracted and was checked only as text; the page images were not inspected.

savings.reason: Paragraph 2 of Executive Order 8854 independently withdraws and reserves the lands that Executive Order 8168 had reserved, together with an adjoining tract, for the Coast and Geodetic Survey. That later reservation is a separate command of Executive Order 8854 and continues independently of the ended Executive Order 8168. No saving clause preserves any provision of Executive Order 8168 itself.
